changes.note: Client Portal: each part has its own page now (Home, Messages, Shop, Website info, Requests). Home shows what needs you first, and a phone has the pages along the bottom. Boxes that pop up are calmer: the page dims and there is one row of buttons. What you edit and save yourself (shop, hours, contact info, social pages) is separate from what you send to Stray Wolf (a new logo, photos, changes to your website). Your shop list is easier to read, with a Status column and a warning when an item has no photo. Website visitors on Home shows each number week by week: four columns with the last 7 days in orange, how the 4 weeks compare with the 4 before, and a few plain lines such as your busiest day and where people found you.

Hours, holidays, email, address and social links now come from her Business info: a change saved in her Client Portal or in Stray Wolf Admin shows on every page within a minute. Holidays and special days in the next two weeks show under the hours, and the open-now line knows about them. A Facebook or Google link shows in the footer once she adds one. In her portal, Shop hours, Contact info and Your social pages open an editor that saves straight to the site. Needs SW Core 2.5.

Accessibility and search pass. The changing photo on Home has a pause button and its caption is no longer read out on a timer. On a phone, keyboard focus stops clear of the bottom bar. The private event form has darker box outlines, a clear focus ring and says which boxes are optional. Gallery tile names stay readable over bright photos and the photo viewer reads out each caption. Shorter page titles for search results, links between pages go straight to the short address, the page list carries a date, the next workshop is offered to Google as an event while it is still ahead, and phones get a home-screen icon. The next workshop's details now live in one place (WS in build.mjs).

Client Portal matches TVIS V14: easier-to-read orange and grey text, plain status tags on your requests, small help tips on the message buttons, and the latest shop manager. Pinch zoom works on phones.

Shop: the DIY Terrarium Kits, Terrarium Bar and Plant Bar tabs follow her shop list. Showing fills in today's price (a sale shows the regular price crossed out) and the checkout link; Sold out puts a Sold out for now note (Fully booked for the Terrarium Bar) in place of Buy; Hidden takes the tab away and the row closes up. Needs SW Core 2.3 and the three items set to Showing.
Visit Us opens on the photographer's photo of Dani at her Fifth Market booth: her face, her sign and her plant care jars, in place of the shop-window photo that cut her off.

Shop and Workshops: each item from her shop can show up to 5 photos to swipe through (arrows and dots), a sale tag with the old price crossed out and the last day, From the lowest price when choices cost different amounts, each option on its own line, New and Featured tags, and Sold out fades the photo.

Client Portal: Contact info, Shop hours and Your social pages are each one tidy list, every row the same height, and each social page has its own logo beside its name (Instagram, Etsy, Facebook, Google).

Home opens in her own words from her current site: Plants that make a house feel like home, her welcome, and Plan your visit and Book a workshop. Visit Us: the photo of Dani at the shop window shows her face.

Client Portal: Your shop is the same shop manager Stray Wolf uses: every item in one list with its photo, price and whether it shows on the website; add, change, sale prices, photos, Undo and a list of changes, download the photos or a spreadsheet. Needs SW Core 2.2.

Home opens tighter: her welcome sits closer under the logo tag and the photo is a little shorter, so the words and the photo line up. Every page gets a very faint leaf pattern and a soft sage wash across the top, so the cream reads less like empty white.

Client Portal: On your site now has a button for each page of the website (All, then each page), with how many photos each has. Tap one to see only that page's photos; Download these saves just those.

The Client Portal matches TVIS: Messages from your website is an inbox (tap a message to open it, one-tap delete with Undo, select several or all, a compact line for where the emails go), Let's talk is a button in the header beside Help and under the welcome next to Edit my website, and the page runs in a new order: what's on your site now (logo, contact info, shop hours, social pages, photos), then Messages, your shop, Edit mode, your requests, the numbers and Let's talk.

The Client Portal's header matches Stray Wolf's other portals: a charcoal Stray Wolf strip with Client Portal, Private and secure, Help and Log out, then a white row with her logo on a small tile, her shop name and the links to each part of the page. On a phone her name gives way to the links.

Home now opens on the photographer's picture of Dani in overalls (the sharpest of all her photos), and About on Dani with the monstera in her Snip & Sprout Co. tee. The menu at the top is set in a soft serif (Lora) beside her logo. The open-now pill turns green with a green dot while the shop is open, and a soft red with a red dot while it's closed.

A calmer, cleaner look. One modern typeface for every page, in place of the tall heading font and the serif text. Every page has its own top: Home opens on her welcome and a new photo of Dani, then the Plant Bar with the four steps from her sign; Shop shows the three things to buy with their prices; Workshops shows the next workshop as a card; Gallery opens on its four groups; Visit Us puts the address, hours and directions on one card; About opens on her hello. Shop is first in the menu, as a button. Her logo tag is sharper, and sits above the blurb in the footer. The scrolling strip of sayings is gone, and the three words on About sit side by side. The footer's columns fit their words, so the hours stay on one line. Behind the scenes, ready for launch: each page names its own address, a link shared in a text or a post shows a picture of her Plant Bar, and there is a list of the pages for search engines (the demo itself still stays out of search).

A Gallery page: 24 of her photos in four groups (Terrariums, The Plant Bar, Workshops, Plants), each with a line in her words. Tap a photo to see it full screen with its caption, and step through them all. Gallery is in the menu, in the phone's bottom bar and under her favorites on Home. The Client Portal shows her shop name at the top, links to each part of the page, and a Download button for her logo.

Her logo in the header is now her olive logo box, hanging from the top of the bar like a shop tag, big enough that every line reads. The footer opens on her shop: the counter and wall shelves with plants, pots and her terrariums, and her watering can going along watering each plant as it grows (with a pause button; still for anyone who asked for less motion). Instagram and Etsy icons in their own colours in the footer (with email and portal icons), and the Instagram icon on the Follow button.
Her own logo (Snip &, SPROUT, PLANT CO.) in the header, the footer and the Client Portal, redrawn in its typeface so it stays sharp at every size. On the portal, "Find us" is now "Address".

Every page now in Dani's own words, taken from her text about the Shop, her Instagram posts, her current site and her Plant Bar sign. The scrolling band shows six of her plant-marker sayings on her dusty rose.

Smaller and tighter: the layout stops growing at a normal desktop width and sits centred, type, photos and spacing a notch smaller on every page, the olive bands and the Shop cards and kit photo tightened. The header is now her sage green, with the open-now line as a pill.
Tidy-up: old photos removed, and the Client Portal's shop card now works with any checkout, not only Square.

Plant Bar menu look: every page opens on a short list set big, like the sign at her Plant Bar (Home: her four steps; Shop: the three ways with prices; Workshops: Gather. Create. Grow.; Visit: the hours, with today marked), beside one photo with a ticket on it. Home adds a slow strip of her plant-marker sayings, the three ways as photo cards and the Plant Bar questions; inner pages read as numbered sections. Photos: her photographer's shots wherever there is one, with the window glare taken off the Plant Bar sign; one gentle, matching finish on her Instagram photos; the Shop's photos at full size so they stay sharp on big screens.

New look: a full-width header with the open-now status, larger type, rounded photos with soft shadows, card layouts, pill buttons, section labels on Home, a full footer with hours and links, and the Stray Wolf badge. The Shop tiles and buy button match.

Simpler pages: the visit planner, the plant quiz, the marker picker, the countdown and the hours chart are gone. Home is now the top, three ways to make something, the next workshop, reviews, the gallery and the visit card.

Design pass: tablet layouts, one left edge on every page, big-screen scaling, two more shop photos and a fuller top on About, the next date on Workshops, and the calendar link on Workshops now visible.
First draft of the new website: Home, Shop, Workshops, Visit, About and the Client Portal.
